target_customer: US military and air defense commanders (government buyers)
problem: Defending against drones and cruise missiles with fighter jets or expensive missiles is too costly; the company wants a fighter-class response at a fraction of the cost.
business_model: Defense hardware sold to government customers (contracts not public)
product_category: Reusable unmanned jet interceptors for air defense

founders.name: Parker Jamieson
prior_employers: US Air Force (11 years as a pilot, F-16 and U-28A evaluator pilot)
education: Ecole de l'air et de l'espace
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page. Operator and pilot background rather than engineering.

founders.name: Christopher Palazzolo
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page: Head of Operations at H3X; over 4 years at Boom rising to Director of Aircraft and Production Operations for the XB-1 demonstrator, leading avionics, flight test and manufacturing.

technical_complexity.rationale: A jet-speed reusable unmanned interceptor with target identification and recovery needs propulsion, avionics, autonomy and flight test, all hardware and certification heavy for a three person team.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware and defense procurement relationships are hard to copy, but well funded interceptor rivals exist.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not yet known; many funded counter-drone startups and Anduril were already building interceptors.

market_need_then: Counter-UAS startups raised over $1.2B across 15 verified rounds between Q1 2025 and Q1 2026 per one tracker, showing demand for low cost interceptors against drones and missiles.

identity.logo: Simple Keres logo on a minimal page
identity.visual_style: Minimal single page with a short tagline
identity.voice_and_tone: Brief, direct and confident; tagline 'Reusable tactical airpower.'

branding.brand_signature: Product name Garmur and the phrase 'Kill the drone, keep the jet'

brand_strength.rationale: Early brand with a memorable one-liner and a distinctive name, but no press about the brand yet.

outcome_analysis: Keres is a Fall 2026 company with an Air Force pilot CEO and a CTO who led production operations at Boom, so it is too early for an outcome. No shutdown, acquisition or layoff news was found. The key risks are the hardware difficulty for a three person team and well funded counter-drone competitors raising large rounds in mid 2026.
notes: Funding: Dealroom lists a $125K seed, seen only on an aggregator with no investors, so unverified and not recorded as a round. Name origin: Keres is also the Greek term for death spirits, but no source ties the company name to it, so name_origin is null. Dealroom's list of the CTO's prior employers (Cosmic Aerospace, United Launch Alliance) differs from the YC page and is not used.
